comment: Rules that no query can make the first match in a configuration where the clause is emitted at that index. These are conditional fallbacks: a broader, feature-gated rule wins when the feature is on, and the same clause is reachable (usually at a different index) when the feature is off. They are not missing questions and not upstream bugs. Rule indices shift when a builder omits a conditional clause; see docs/EVIDENCE-riscv.md.

gaps.follow_up: conditional fallback: reachable when Zfa is off (the libcall is then rule 0 and is witnessed). No upstream action.
gaps.reason: shadowed in ristretto (the only Zfa configuration): legalFor(Zfa, {s32}) and legalFor(Zfa && D, {s64}) match the same result types earlier, so the libcallFor({s32, s64}) clause can never be the first match. In configurations without Zfa the clause is emitted as the first libcall rule and is witnessed.

gaps.follow_up: conditional fallback if a configuration without D appears; all current configurations enable D. No upstream action.
gaps.reason: libcallFor({s64, s32}) is subsumed by the earlier legalFor(D, {{s64, s32}}); every one of the 8 configurations enables D, so this clause can never be the first match.

gaps.follow_up: conditional fallback for the Zfhmin-off case; reachable at a different index there. No upstream action.
gaps.reason: libcallFor({{s16,s32},{s16,s64},{s32,s64}}) is subsumed when Zfhmin is on: legalFor(Zfhmin, {s16,s32}), legalFor(Zfhmin && D, {s16,s64}) and legalFor(D, {s32,s64}) cover all three pairs earlier. Configurations without Zfhmin do not emit this clause at this index.

gaps.follow_up: ordering artifact: reachable only when the earlier condition is absent (rv32), where it is witnessed at a different index. No upstream action.
gaps.reason: two clauses share this index. Without Zfh it is narrowScalarFor({s64, f16}), but widenScalarIf(f16 && !Zfh) rewrites the source to s32 first. With Zfh the index is that widenScalarIf clause, whose predicate is false because !Zfh fails. Unreachable in either case.
